The excerpt effectively uses the compression of time to provide a rich and necessary exposition for the story. Within just two paragraphs, the author (Arthur Schnitzler, in the opening of *Casanovas Heimfahrt*) condenses the last ten years of Casanova’s exile, his gradual aging and psychological shift from defiance to desperate homesickness, and his recent two-month stay in Mantua. This manipulation of time feels completely balanced and appropriate because it serves to establish the protagonist's current state of mind and circumstances—much like the metaphor used in the text of a bird circling in ever-narrowing loops—smoothly bringing the narrative from a broad overview of his past years down to his immediate present at the inn.
